name: FishMonger’s arsenal upgraded: SprySOCKS for Windows.
description: ESET researchers have identified two undocumented Windows variants of the FishMonger backdoor, SprySOCKS, which was previously known only in its Linux iteration. These Windows variants, designated as WIN_DRV and WIN_PLUS, have demonstrated active usage targeting government organizations across Honduras, Taiwan, Thailand, and Pakistan from 2023 to 2024. Both variants operate with a hardcoded command and control (C&C) configuration that supports communication via TCP, UDP, and WebSocket protocols and can execute over 30 C&C commands, including file management and system information retrieval.

name: Earth Lusca Uses KTLVdoor Backdoor for Multiplatform Intrusion
description: A new multiplatform backdoor named KTLVdoor, written in Golang with versions for Windows and Linux, has been discovered during monitoring of the Chinese-speaking threat actor Earth Lusca. This highly obfuscated malware impersonates system utilities and allows attackers to control infected systems, manipulate files, and gather information. The campaign involves over 50 C&C servers hosted in China, potentially shared with other threat actors. KTLVdoor uses sophisticated encryption and obfuscation techniques, including a custom TLV-like configuration format and AES-GCM encryption for C&C communication. The malware's capabilities include file operations, command execution, port scanning, and proxy functionality.
